originalConstitution.proposal: Cardano Constitution to Replace the Interim Constitution
originalConstitution.overallSentiment: Broadly supportive with pragmatic acceptance of imperfection
argumentsFor: Reflected the will of delegates at the Buenos Aires Constitutional Convention in Argentina
Major step up from the Interim Constitution — replaces an imperfect placeholder with a delegate-endorsed document
Interim Constitution may have required this draft to be in place before alternatives could be proposed
Constitution is a living document — amendable over time, not a permanent final text
Establishes 10 Cardano Blockchain Tenets and a dedicated Treasury Budget article
Reinforces three-body governance model (DReps, SPOs, CC) with checks and balances
Redistributes governance power from the 3 founding entities (IOG, CF, Emurgo) to ADA holders
Strong incentives for community to act in good faith tied to ADA price appreciation
Provides foundation for liquid democracy and on-chain governance tools
argumentsAgainst: 1 lovelace = 1 vote model is plutocratic and excludes smaller holders
Document too long and complex — risks creating Cardano bureaucracy
Lack of clear definitions invites ambiguous interpretation
500 ADA DRep deposit is too high, especially for participants in developing countries
100,000 ADA govDeposit for governance actions is an extreme barrier — no pooling tools available
Off-chain governance given too prominent a role
Constitutional Committee given too much prominence in a decentralized system
Gov.tools limitations meant no competing constitution could be submitted
Africa and other underrepresented regions have less than 2% governance representation
No mechanism for quadratic voting or DID-based identity — governance centralized from the start
Overly precise parameter guardrails should ideally be set by individual votes
controversialClauses: Article 1 Section 1 Tenet 9 and Article 2 Section 2 — seen as violated by high deposit requirements
Article 3 Section 5 — alternative to gov.tools not ready, perceived violation
1 token = 1 vote model codified — prevents future alternative governance models
notableNOVotes: some anonymous DReps citing process concerns
notableYESVotes: GAIA (Yes with extensive concerns about tooling and deposit barriers)
originalConstitution.consensusView: Near-universal YES with the understanding this is a minimum viable starting point, not a finished product

Staggering CC member terms — unclear how this works given ledger only recognizes one CC
Disclosure requirements for multi-role holders (DRep+SPO) seen as unenforceable

Ada Holder vs Ada Owner terminology debate begins

NO: Eternl DRep Committee (detailed line-by-line criticism of unenforceable clauses and grammatical errors)

changes: Continued refinement from v2.0, incorporating DRep feedback
More clarity on Net Change Limit

controversies: EMURGO voted NO: revised NCL weakens explicit link between approved budgets and treasury withdrawals

CRITICAL vs SECURITY parameter category confusion in guardrails (Cerkoryn noted)

changes: Reverted 'Ada Holder' back to 'Ada Owner' (compromise to unblock process)

v2_4.significance: EMURGO's reversal from NO (v2.3) to YES (v2.4) signals that the Ada Owner reversion and removal of unenforceable clauses addressed their core concerns

crossVersionThemes: The Budget Info Action removal was consistently debated — most DReps ultimately supported removing it as reducing bureaucracy
Enforceability is a recurring theme: DRep disclosure requirements, SPO overlap disclosure, and Codes of Conduct all flagged as unenforceable
YUTA as author received broad credit for responsive engagement with community feedback across all versions

replacingInterimCC.result: Broad YES support — seen as milestone in decentralization
keyPoints: Transitions from appointed (IOG, CF, Emurgo, Intersect) to community-elected members
Process was on-chain with public audits and full documentation
Cardano Foundation recused two members (Nicolas Cerny and Matthias Benkort) due to their CC candidacy
HOSKY: replaces centralized control with elected governance — prevents 'governance vacuum'
EMURGO: smooth transition, confident in new CC's ability to uphold constitution
replacingInterimCC.unanimity: Near-unanimous YES — one of the most broadly supported structural actions

firstAddition.note: Intersect held off-chain vote, community chose Cardano Curia for the vacant seat
firstAddition.support: Broadly supported — Cerkoryn noted fair process

christinaAddition.controversy: Runner-up in Intersect snap election — disputed whether adding runner-up is valid
argumentsFor: Ekklesia poll showed community support
Extra CC member above minimum provides resilience buffer
Prevents governance paralysis when members resign
CC role is thankless — more volunteers are beneficial
argumentsAgainst: EMURGO voted NO: election was conducted for ONE seat, Curia was clear winner
Constitutionally ambiguous — document doesn't clearly permit expanding beyond replacement
Expanding from 7 to 8 changes decision thresholds
Potential unplanned compensation costs
christinaAddition.split: YES majority but with notable dissent from EMURGO on procedural grounds

reducingMinSize_7to5.context: One CC member retired unexpectedly, causing governance stall in December 2025
argumentsFor: Provides safety margin — committee remains functional if 2 members resign unexpectedly
Prevents governance paralysis experienced when a member retired
Lowering minimum does not change percentage required to ratify actions
Cerkoryn: reduces minimum, does not necessarily reduce actual size
InputEndorsers: pragmatic — if not ideal, can always hold new election and increase size later
reducingMinSize_7to5.caveat: Cardano Foundation noted a 'root-reference' technical conflict (memory units proposal passed first), making this technically invalidated. Also warned that committee of 5 requires only 2 dissenting votes to block action (vs 3 for committee of 7)

ccCompensation.proposal: 200,000 ADA per seat for Epochs 581-653 (total ~1M ADA)
argumentsFor: Constitution anticipates key governance roles should be fairly compensated
Fair compensation ensures qualified and unbiased individuals can dedicate necessary time
Accountability for public resources is non-negotiable — CC role is substantial work
InputEndorsers: CC should serve as independent barrier to governance capture
argumentsAgainst: Cardano Foundation (NO): Improper sequencing — compensation before accountability framework
High pre-determined amount risks attracting candidates motivated by payment rather than duty
No calculation provided for 200k ADA per seat figure
High workload is a governance design flaw — fix the design, don't compensate for structural bottleneck
EMURGO (ABSTAIN): unclear if 1M ADA figure is for total or per-seat, need shared information space
Cerkoryn (NO): too much too soon, should be supplementary income not a full-time salary
ccCompensation.HOSKYNote: ABSTAINED explicitly due to conflict of interest as a CC member
ccCompensation.outcome: Contentious — CF and Cerkoryn voted NO, EMURGO and HOSKY abstained, InputEndorsers voted YES

nclAnalysis.overview: The Net Change Limit was one of the most contested areas of governance. Multiple competing proposals appeared simultaneously, with DReps divided over appropriate level and methodology.

initialNCL_350M_2025.CFPosition: YES — constitutional prerequisite, grounded in previous year's inflows
initialNCL_350M_2025.HOSKYPosition: NO — sets limit too high, frames cap as target, sends wrong fiscal signal
initialNCL_350M_2025.CerkorynPosition: NO — excessively high, no governance maturity yet to justify, risks incentivizing max withdrawal
initialNCL_350M_2025.EMURGOPosition: YES — 2025 is a critical transition year, flexibility needed for emerging regulatory opportunities

competingNCL_300M_and_250M_2025_2026.proposal: Set 2025 NCL of 300M ADA, 2026 NCL of 250M ADA
competingNCL_300M_and_250M_2025_2026.CFPosition: NO — undermines stability of already-approved 350M 2025 NCL, premature 2026 definition

NCL_300M_563to635.proposal: Set a 300 million ADA Net Change Limit for Epochs 563-635
NCL_300M_563to635.CFPosition: NO — altering ratified NCL mid-year undermines governance stability and trust
NCL_300M_563to635.CerkorynPosition: YES — after 200M proposal failed, switched to YES as compromise: tighter than 350M while covering approved budgets, ADA price up ~50% enabling further restraint

NCL_2025Cardano_200M.CerkorynPosition: YES — fiscally responsible midpoint, preserves/grows treasury while existing 350M keeps process open, tighter cap forces better proposals

NCL_613to713_350M.proposal: Net Change Limit (Epoch 613 to Epoch 713) — 350M ADA for ~16.5 months
NCL_613to713_350M.CFPosition: YES — operational necessity, corrects governance calendar, incorporates unspent stablecoin budget, annualized rate lower than previous year
NCL_613to713_350M.EMURGOPosition: YES — constitutional requirement, duration realignment is meaningful governance improvement
NCL_613to713_350M.CerkorynPosition: NO — reserve dwindling, ADA at $0.33 limits USD leverage, 2030 Vision not refined enough for comfort
NCL_613to713_350M.InputEndorsersPosition: ABSTAIN — NCLs are performative theater; real battles are individual treasury withdrawals
NCL_613to713_350M.keyCritique_InputEndorsers: NCLs as social consensus performed 12-18 months in advance don't limit anything — if majority wants to extend/increase, they will. The real governance work is scrutinizing individual withdrawals.

NCL_300M_613to713.proposal: Net Change Limit of 300 Million ADA for Epochs 613-713
NCL_300M_613to713.CerkorynPosition: YES — prefers 300M over 350M, dwindling reserve and ADA price concerns

coreDebateDimensions: Is 300M too high or too low? Fiscal conservatives (HOSKY, Cerkoryn) say too high; CF and EMURGO accept it as data-backed
Should NCL be based on inflows (CF: yes, grounded in empirical data) or strategic spending need (Cerkoryn: spending should reflect value delivered not inflow capacity)?
Are NCLs meaningful governance tools or 'performative theater'? InputEndorsers provocatively argued the latter
Multi-year vs single-year NCLs: CF initially preferred 1-year then endorsed longer period for calendar alignment
Should approved NCLs be revisited mid-cycle? CF strongly argued NO (governance stability); others said YES if needed
300M_arguments_too_high: Signals that maximum is the target, not a ceiling
Treasury reserve is dwindling, emissions declining
ADA price in USD gives limited real-world leverage
Governance system still immature — no robust oversight to justify level
Fiscal conservatism should be signaled at the framework level
Approving 100% of last year's income sends the wrong message (HOSKY)
300M_arguments_appropriate: Grounded in realized inflows, provides empirical basis
Constitutional prerequisite — without NCL, all treasury withdrawals blocked
Covers approved budgets while being noticeably lower than 350M ceiling
Annualized rate for longer-period NCL is actually lower than previous year
Carries over authority for previously approved unspent stablecoin budget
All withdrawals still subject to separate scrutiny and 67% approval threshold

budgetProcessAnalysis.proposal: Cardano Budget Process Framework (facilitated by Intersect)
budgetProcessAnalysis.overallSentiment: Generally positive but with specific critiques about process clarity and Intersect centralization
supportArguments: Strategic alignment to 2030 Strategic Pillars and ecosystem KPIs is a needed improvement
Work package-based budgeting allows DReps to compare outcomes directly
1,000 ADA donation and 100,000 ADA minimum threshold deter low-effort submissions
67% Ekklesia threshold is improvement over previous 50% threshold (Cerkoryn)
Milestone-based smart contract disbursement improves accountability
Multi-party checks and balances and milestone tracking align with responsible treasury stewardship
critiques: InputEndorsers voted NO: Ekklesia voting process critically underspecified — how long will it last? How is 67% calculated per proposal vs session? What is minimum DRep participation threshold? How are passive abstentions counted? Too much interpretive power left to Intersect
Static 100k ADA minimum risks artificially inflating project costs (CF recommendation)
Cardano Foundation caution about centralization of admin duties — this is not the ONLY way to request treasury funding
Need for SME support for DReps evaluating highly technical proposals (CF)
Large institutional DReps with Intersect presence have participation advantages over small DReps (InputEndorsers)
No RFP-style process — open-ended proposals less efficient than defined RFPs (CF recommendation)
Budget cycle should start earlier (CF recommendation)

budgetProcessAnalysis.intersectRole: Intersect facilitated and submitted largest budget in 2025; centralization concerns are recurring

increaseMemoryUnits.support: Near-unanimous YES — one of the most straightforward technical votes
arguments: Clear developer experience benefits — allows more complex Plutus scripts without inefficient workarounds

Block diffusion remains well within 5-second 95% propagation target
Part 1 of 2 structure required by Constitutional Guardrails (MTEU-M-04) — maximum increase per epoch
CF advocates bundling parameter changes to reduce SPO voting burden

decreaseTreasuryTax.parameter: treasuryCut (tau / treasury_growth_rate) — all three names refer to the same parameter
decreaseTreasuryTax.background: IOG researchers originally recommended 5% at Shelley launch, but parameter was set to 20%. Effective rate is ~33% due to total stake calculation vs active stake
supportArguments: Treasury has had sufficient time to accumulate value
Small increase in rewards for delegators and SPOs is better use than treasury growth at this stage
Cerkoryn: voted YES but preferred incremental reduction rather than sudden 10% drop
oppositionArguments: Cardano Foundation (NO): No multi-year projections, no bear market scenario modeling, inflated APY baseline overstates benefits, halving treasury tax is a drastic change
CF requested: 5-year multi-year treasury projections, staking simulations with agent-based modeling, inflation analysis, reversion/recovery plan with defined triggers
InputEndorsers (NO): Wants gradual reduction, not a sharp swing. 'Financial predictability and gradual change' is how global financial systems should evolve. Will support future gradual decrease.
HOSKY position not observed in files read
decreaseTreasuryTax.controversy: CF's NO was not opposition to reducing tau, but opposition to doing so without sufficient financial modeling
decreaseTreasuryTax.split: Contested — significant YES support but CF and InputEndorsers voted NO

LloydDuhon: While appreciating HOSKY's contributions, the community needs to develop collaboration muscles and communicate before raising proposals
Cerkoryn: Counter-proposed naming it 'Sadosky Hard Fork' after Argentine mathematician Manuel Sadosky — rhymes with 'Hosky' and honors the host country of the Constitutional Convention

HOSKYHardFork.spirit: Affectionate toward HOSKY as a community institution, but firm on governance norms

LloydDuhon: 'RIP Matthew Plomin. He was an amazing contributor to our ecosystem and a person I considered a friend... Much love to Jillian and the children.'
Cardano Foundation: Matthew was a delegate at the Buenos Aires Constitutional Convention, co-lead of CC Election Working Group, primary driving force behind Article VIII, and a dedicated DRep

vanRossemHardFork.context: Protocol Version 11 named after Max van Rossem, another passed community member
sentiments: Cardano Foundation: Max was integral to election of first elected CC, contributed to constitution development, founding AdaMoments project, facilitated Dutch community meetups

Cerkoryn: 'Naming the next hard fork after him seems like the least we can do to honor him'

hardForkNaming.pattern: The hard fork naming episode reveals an important governance norm: DReps will enforce data integrity and process standards even for beloved community figures (HOSKY), but will unite quickly around human tributes to those who served the ecosystem (Plomin, van Rossem)

notableQuotes.quote: NCLs are in reality a bit of performative theater mandated by the constitution... There is literally no one who knows the ideal NCL today. It could be 150 Million ADA, it could be 250 Million ADA. Or it could be 400 Million ADA if we are to integrate the NASDAQ in 2026.

notableQuotes.quote: Our constitutions are but snapshots in time of an ephemeral consensus — not a national constitution. They can and should be improved by the community without waiting for one of the big entities to spearhead the process. Evolution waits for no one.

notableQuotes.proposal: Rename the Chang 2 Hard Fork to the Plomin Hard Fork

notableQuotes.quote: The removal of non-binding 'expectations' (such as Codes of Conduct) clarifies the document's purpose: it is a set of hard rules for the ledger, not a social manifesto. This focus on enforceability is a necessary evolution for long-term stability.

notableQuotes.quote: Approving an NCL equal to 100 percent of last year's treasury income sends the wrong message. Until we have stronger data on actual funding needs, outcomes, and transaction volume growth, setting the NCL this high is not just unnecessary, it is the opposite of conservative.

notableQuotes.quote: A tighter cap protects the protocol while on-chain governance, auditing, and budgeting mechanisms are still in their infancy, ensuring we learn and iterate under controlled risk rather than spending aggressively before the guardrails are battle-tested.
notableQuotes.significance: Best articulation of the conservative spending case during governance infancy

themes.description: Across all constitution versions, the dominant improvement trend was removing unenforceable provisions (Codes of Conduct, disclosure requirements, overlap declarations) and replacing them with hard ledger rules. By v2.4, CF articulated this explicitly: 'a set of hard rules for the ledger, not a social manifesto.'

themes.theme: Budget Info Action as Bureaucratic Redundancy
themes.description: The removal of the mandatory Budget Info Action was consistently supported across v2.0, v2.3, and v2.4 as reducing governance fatigue and bureaucracy, while integrating requirements directly into Treasury Withdrawals. EMURGO's initial concern (that removal weakens fiscal link) was addressed in v2.4's enhanced per-withdrawal accountability.

A persistent tension between how governance actions are created (in-person conventions vs asynchronous community review) and whether the resulting document is substantively better. CF resolved this by focusing purely on substance; others (like EMURGO on v2.0) were concerned process shortcuts undermined legitimacy.

Multiple DReps (Cerkoryn, HOSKY on NCL, CF on treasury tax, InputEndorsers on treasury tax) consistently argued for caution before the governance system's oversight mechanisms are 'battle-tested.' The lack of proven ROI from treasury spending is a recurring concern.

Repeated concern across budget process, CC compensation, and NCL discussions about Intersect having too much interpretive power, administrative authority, and visibility advantage over non-Intersect participants. InputEndorsers named this explicitly: large institutional DReps with Intersect presence have a structural participation advantage.

themes.theme: Governance as Living System, Not Sacred Text
themes.description: Almost universal agreement that the constitution should be iteratively improved — 'snapshot in time of an ephemeral consensus' (InputEndorsers). This framing enables pragmatic YES votes even with reservations, because today's flaws can be fixed tomorrow.

themes.theme: Human Tribute via Hard Fork Naming
themes.description: Hard fork naming has organically evolved into a community tribute mechanism for fallen contributors. The HOSKY Hard Fork failure and subsequent unanimous tributes to Plomin and van Rossem demonstrate a norm: personal contributions to governance earn posthumous recognition; meme-based proposals face procedural scrutiny.

InputEndorsers' provocative framing has merit: NCLs have been revised mid-cycle, extended, and effectively renegotiated when majorities wanted different limits. The real spending decisions happen at individual withdrawal level with 67% approval. The NCL is a ceiling that the community will adjust as needed.

The 1 token = 1 vote model, high deposit barriers, and geographic underrepresentation (Africa < 2%) are systemic concerns raised by multiple DReps. The governance system was designed with plutocratic tendencies baked in, and the concern that whales will resist reform of voting power distribution is existential.

Reduction of redundant votes (Budget Info Action removal, CC size reduction for operational resilience) is consistently supported to manage DRep cognitive load. The Eternl DRep Committee's detailed editorial critique of v2.0 illustrates the work DReps are expected to do — and the practical limits of that expectation at scale.

insights: The constitution debate is fundamentally about speed vs rigor: the YES majority adopted a pragmatic 'minimum viable governance' stance, accepting imperfect documents to keep the process moving, while NO voters demanded more careful deliberation. The Chilean experience (Rodrigo-CHIL) and Cardano Foundation's 'net positive' test both resolved this tension in favor of forward momentum.

YUTA has become the de facto constitutional maintenance lead — credited by EMURGO, InputEndorsers, and Cerkoryn for responsive, iterative improvement. This informal role lacks constitutional basis and creates a single point of dependency.

The Eternl DRep Committee's detailed v2.0 NO vote — citing grammar, capitalization, unenforceability — represents a quality standard that the community implicitly adopted. Later versions addressed most of these issues, suggesting DRep line-item feedback has real influence.

EMURGO's v2.3 NO to v2.4 YES flip on the 'Ada Owner' terminology compromise reveals how large institutional DReps can be moved by targeted specific concessions — the whole amendment process essentially unblocked on a terminology choice.

The CC compensation debate exposed a governance design problem: the Constitutional Committee's workload is high, its quorum requirements are brittle, and there is no accountability framework. The CF's 'fix the design, not the compensation' argument addresses a structural problem that DReps will be forced to revisit.

HOSKY's fiscal conservatism on the NCL reveals a governance tension: the most populist and 'meme-adjacent' DRep by reputation is one of the most fiscally conservative voices in practice, voting NO on the 350M NCL and consistently emphasizing that the limit should signal restraint not possibility.

The governance system has successfully handled multiple governance crises in quick succession: the December 2025 CC member retirement halting governance, the NCL mid-cycle revision debate, the Christina addition controversy. Each revealed protocol gaps that were then addressed through new governance actions — demonstrating resilience.

The Input Endorsers' description of NCLs as 'performative theater' is the most intellectually honest critique in the dataset. NCL has been revised at will when majorities wanted different limits — the true constraint on treasury spending is the 67% withdrawal threshold, not the NCL ceiling.

Hard fork naming is a low-stakes arena where DReps simultaneously enforce governance norms (data integrity, process compliance) and express community values (tribute to fallen contributors). The HOSKY Hard Fork failure was not a rejection of HOSKY as a community figure but a statement that governance proposals must meet minimum metadata standards.

The three founding entities (IOG, CF, Emurgo) have transitioned from controlling the CC to participating as DReps — a genuine decentralization milestone. Their diverse positions (CF and Emurgo sometimes voting differently from each other and from the majority) show the governance system is beginning to function with genuine pluralism.
